note.note:
Consult Summary:
- 35-year-old male lawyer with months of low mood, low energy, decreased appetite, intermittent nausea and headaches, and ~1 stone unintentional weight loss over ≥6 months; episodic palpitations/shortness of breath in lifts but not with walking; history of hypothyroidism off levothyroxine for months. Plan: initial blood tests; safety-netting provided.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Low appetite and energy; feeling “down”; intermittent nausea and headaches; episodes of palpitations and feeling unable to breathe in lifts; unintentional weight loss.
- Timeline:
  - Appetite decreased: ~3–3.5 months.
  - Weight loss: ~1 stone (~6.3 kg) over at least 6 months.
  - Low mood/low energy: ongoing for “long, long” time (months).
  - Palpitations/SOB: occur notably in lifts; not associated with walking.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Triggers: Lifts/elevators. Not exertional. No specific food triggers for nausea.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Nausea without vomiting.
  - Headaches at work.
  - Wife notes issues with “nightly activities” (suggests reduced sexual function/libido).
  - Reports ability to walk a mile without dyspnea; later notes he has not been walking much recently, making exertional tolerance uncertain.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No chest pain.
  - No cough.
  - No diarrhea; no blood or mucus in stool.
  - Bowels “OK”; no pain with defecation.
  - No known acid reflux.
  - No specific home or work stressors endorsed; changed law firm ~3.5 months ago.

Past Medical History:
- Hypothyroidism (underactive thyroid).
  - Previously on levothyroxine; stopped taking it since changing doctor (months ago).
  - No recent thyroid blood tests; “hasn’t taken one in a long time.”

Medications:
- Levothyroxine (thyroxine) — stopped; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Current medications: Not documented.
- Allergies: Not documented.

Social History:
- Occupation: Lawyer; changed law firm ~3.5 months ago.
- Activity: Markedly reduced recent walking/physical activity.
- Home: Lives with wife; relationship issues noted around sexual function.
- Tobacco/alcohol/substances: Not recorded.

Family History:
- Not recorded.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not recorded (telehealth).
- Examination findings: Not recorded.

Investigations:
- Tests ordered/planned: “General set of bloods” including screening for anemia (CBC), kidney function, liver function, vitamin levels, and thyroid function tests. Patient instructed to call support via app to arrange blood draw; will receive text to book follow-up once results are available.
- Imaging: None mentioned.
- Results: None available.

Assessment & Plan:
- Overall Impression:
  - Subacute constitutional symptoms (low appetite, fatigue, weight loss) with low mood and situational palpitations/SOB in lifts. History of hypothyroidism off replacement. Initial plan is broad lab evaluation; no immediate red flags on history.

- DDx Integration (brief):
  - Major depressive disorder or mixed anxiety/depression: Low mood, anhedonia-like statements, low energy, decreased appetite, weight loss, sexual difficulties; functioning reduced. No formal diagnosis made in visit.
  - Hypothyroidism relapse due to stopping levothyroxine: Known history; off medication for months; symptoms compatible (fatigue, low mood), though weight loss less typical.
  - Situational panic/claustrophobia: Palpitations and dyspnea specifically in lifts; preserved exertional tolerance (initially reported).

- Issue 1: Unintentional weight loss, decreased appetite, fatigue, low mood
  - Plan:
    - Proceed with ordered blood tests: anemia screen, kidney and liver function, vitamin levels, and thyroid function tests.
    - If bloods are normal or inconclusive, arrange in-person physical examination.
    - Safety net: If new red flags occur (persistent vomiting, change in bowel habits, chest pain, persistent/worsening palpitations), seek urgent care/A&E or contact the clinic.
    - Follow-up will be prompted via text once results are back; patient advised to contact clinic sooner if feeling more unwell.

- Issue 2: History of hypothyroidism; medication nonadherence
  - Plan:
    - Check thyroid function tests as part of current labs.
    - Further management to be determined after results.

- Issue 3: Episodic palpitations/shortness of breath in lifts (non-exertional)
  - Plan:
    - Monitor symptoms pending blood test results.
    - Safety net: Seek urgent care/A&E if chest pain develops, if palpitations are severe or persistent, or if shortness of breath worsens.

- General plan items:
  - Patient to call support number in app to arrange blood test.
  - Will receive text to book follow-up appointment when results are available.
  - Advised to re-contact the service if symptoms change or worsen before results.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Allergies, complete medication list (current meds), vital signs, full review of systems (sleep, fevers/night sweats), mental health screening (PHQ/GAD), substance use (tobacco/alcohol/drugs), sexual history details, family history.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx: None explicit. Note: Physician commented that some symptoms (palpitations, weight loss) are less typical for hypothyroidism; DDx still includes hypothyroidism relapse as possible due to medication cessation.
- Transcript quality: Several unclear/inaudible segments and incomplete statements; some timing/quantities are approximate.
